note: Attacker-controlled .gnu_debuglink section data (an empty, corrupted link string) is read from the input file into ptr.
The corrupted string is NUL-terminated inside the section so it passes _dwarf_check_string_valid; its length (0) is accepted without any minimum-length check.
The empty string pointer is returned as the debuglink path name.
The empty debuglink string is passed as link_string_in into _dwarf_construct_linkedto_path.
Appending the empty string is a no-op, so js_linkstring keeps the static one-byte "" literal buffer with no separate allocation; the corrupted (empty) path name is never rejected.
The empty linkname is joined onto the directory path, forwarding it into _dwarf_pathjoinl.
is_full_path() is invoked with inputs pointing at the one-byte empty string literal.
path[0] is NUL (not the joinchar) so path[1] is read one byte past the end of the one-byte static string, an out-of-bounds read that faults (global-buffer-overflow / segmentation violation).
